::: {.lead}
Today you market Mona's Cakes, the service of Lectures 9 and 10. Each
experiment has two parts. **Part A** is in an AI assistant, a search
engine and Canva (a free design tool). **Part B** is on a simulator of the
interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its
link. After each step, write your result in its box. At the end, copy your
key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with a browser, an AI assistant that the
  university allows (for example Microsoft Copilot with your university
  account), and a free Canva account (`canva.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · The audience and the message

**The idea:** **e-marketing** tells people on the Internet about a service.
First choose the **audience**: who the message is for (families in Amman
with a birthday soon). Then the **message**: a headline for them, the
**benefit** (why it helps them), the **offer** (10% off this week) and the
**call to action** (*Order now*, with the link).

**Aim:** choose a message with all its parts.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant)**
:::

1. Copy the prompt into an AI assistant and read the three texts.

   ::: {.prompt}
   Write three short posts for Instagram for Mona's Cakes, a home bakery
   in Amman. The audience is families with a birthday soon. Each post has
   at most 20 words, the offer "10% off birthday cakes this week" and the
   words "Order now". Number the posts 1, 2 and 3.
   :::

   {{< record "The number of the best post" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good post has the audience, the benefit, the offer and the call to
   action, for example: *Birthday soon? Fresh cakes made at home in Amman.
   10% off this week. Order now!* The AI can forget a part: check it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI wrote three posts. Which one has the benefit, the offer and the
   call to action?

   - [x] Birthday soon? Fresh cakes made at home in Amman. 10% off this week. Order now!

     Why: It has the audience, the benefit, the offer and the call to action.

   - [ ] Mona's Cakes is a bakery. We like cakes.

     Why: No benefit for the customer, no offer, no call to action.

   - [ ] 10% off!!! Best cakes in the world!!!

     Why: No call to action, and big words instead of a benefit.
   :::

2. In the best post, find the **call to action**.

   {{< record "The call to action" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Order now**: the words that tell the reader what to do next.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which part of the message? Sort the parts.

   the benefit
   :   Fresh cakes made at home in Amman.

       Why: Why it is good for the customer.

   the offer
   :   10% off this week.

       Why: A reason to act now.

   the call to action
   :   Order now!

       Why: What to do next.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/message-builder.html" poster="sims/message-builder.png" title="Message Builder: the right message for the audience" >}}

3. In **Message Builder**, build Mona's post part by part. Who is the
   audience?

   {{< record "The audience" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Families in Amman with a birthday soon**: a clear group of people.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which audience is clear for Mona's post?

   - [x] families in Amman with a birthday soon

     Why: A clear group with a need: the post speaks to them.

   - [ ] everybody in the world

     Why: Too wide: the post speaks to nobody.

   - [ ] other cake shops

     Why: They do not buy cakes from Mona.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · The channels

**The idea:** a **channel** is the way the message reaches people:
**search engines** (people who search "cakes Amman"; the map of the
shops), **social media** (photos and posts for followers), **e-mail**
(people who already know you) and **paid ads** (you pay, and the ad shows
to the people that you choose; search engines mark them *Sponsored*).

**Aim:** find the channels in a search, and choose a channel for a goal.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (a search engine)**
:::

1. In a browser, search for `cake shop Amman`. Look at the first results.

   {{< record "The word on the paid results" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Sponsored** (or *Ad*): these are paid ads. The other results are free
   results of the search.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A search result has the word *Sponsored*. What is it?

   - [x] a paid ad

     Why: The shop paid to show it at the top.

   - [ ] the best shop

     Why: It is first because it paid, not because it is the best.

   - [ ] a post of a friend

     Why: Posts of friends are on social media.
   :::

2. Find the **map** with the shops on it.

   {{< record "Does the map show the shops with their phone and hours: yes or no?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Yes**: a shop adds itself to the map for free (for example with a
   Google Business Profile). People near it find it there.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Mona wants people who search near her to find her shop for free. Where?

   - [x] on the map of the search engine

     Why: A free listing shows her shop, phone and hours.

   - [ ] in a paid ad only

     Why: The map listing is free.

   - [ ] in an e-mail

     Why: E-mail reaches people who already know her.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/channel-mixer.html" poster="sims/channel-mixer.png" title="Channel Mixer: the right channel for the goal" >}}

3. In **Channel Mixer**, choose the channel for each goal. Which channel
   reaches Mona's 200 old customers for free?

   {{< record "The channel for old customers" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **E-mail**: it reaches the people who already know her, for free.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which channel? Sort the goals.

   search engine
   :   People who search "cakes Amman" must find Mona.

       Why: They search, so they are ready to buy.

   e-mail
   :   The old customers must hear about the new cake.

       Why: E-mail reaches people who know her, for free.

   paid ad
   :   New families must see the offer in three days, with 20 JD.

       Why: A paid ad reaches chosen people fast.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A post and its results

**The idea:** a **promotional post** is a picture with the message: a good
photo, a few words and the call to action. **Canva** (free) has ready-made
designs. Use your own photo or a **free picture**, and write its source.
After a week, **measure**: views, clicks and orders. **Clicks for every
100 views** = clicks ÷ views × 100.

**Aim:** make a post, and read its results.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Canva)**
:::

1. Open `canva.com`, search for **Instagram post** and open a design
   (template) about food. Change its text to: *Birthday cakes made at home
   · 10% off this week · Order now*. Click **Share › Download** (PNG).

   {{< record "The type of the downloaded file" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **PNG**: a picture file, ready to post.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which file do you post on Instagram?

   - [x] the PNG picture

     Why: A post is a picture.

   - [ ] the Canva link

     Why: People see the picture, not your design file.

   - [ ] a Word file

     Why: Social media shows pictures and videos.
   :::

2. In the design, click the photo, then **Elements › Photos** and choose a
   free photo of a cake. Under the post, the source line is *Photo:
   Canva*.

   {{< record "May I use a photo from Google Images: yes or no?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **No**: a picture found on the Internet belongs to someone. Use your own
   photos or free pictures (Canva, Pixabay, Unsplash), with their source.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which picture may Mona use in her post?

   - [x] a free photo from Canva, with "Photo: Canva"

     Why: Free pictures may be used; write the source.

   - [ ] a photo of a famous cake from Google Images

     Why: It belongs to someone else.

   - [ ] the logo of a famous cake company

     Why: A logo belongs to its company.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/results-reader.html" poster="sims/results-reader.png" title="Results Reader: which post worked better?" >}}

3. In **Results Reader**, compare two posts. Post B: 500 views and 25
   clicks. How many clicks for every 100 views?

   {{< record "Post B: … clicks for every 100 views" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **5**: 25 ÷ 500 × 100 = 5. Post A has only 2, so post B worked better.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="5" unit="clicks" hint="500 views is 5 × 100: divide 25 by 5."}
   Post B: 500 views and 25 clicks. How many clicks for every 100 views?

   Why: 25 ÷ 500 × 100 = 5.
   :::
